# ci-compute-local

**Run a substage's targets on this machine and harvest what forge produced.**

A forge-ci `compute` engine.

## Why it exists

This is what makes the tenet true. What runs in CI runs locally, because locally
is the only place it runs.

After a forge target it reads `.forge/artifact-store.yaml` from the directory
forge ran in, so every test report and artifact lands in CI state for free.

## Tools

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `declare` | Report the resources this compute target needs. It needs none. |
| `run` | Run the targets and return the outcome. |

## By hand

```sh
echo '{"revision":"abc","stage":"build","substage":"default","root":"/work","targets":[{"alias":"build-all","forge":"test-all","in":["my-repo"]}]}' \
  | ci-compute-local run
```

## In a pipeline

```yaml
engines:
  - alias: my-compute
    type: compute
    engine: "go://github.com/alexandremahdhaoui/forge-ci/cmd/ci-compute-local@v0.1.4"
    manager: local
```

## Worth knowing

A failing target is **not** an error. It returns `status: failed`. An error means
the machinery broke, not that the code did.

It harvests only reports that started after the run did. forge's store keeps
every past run, so without that filter a run of three stages reports seventy.

`params` are templated in as `{{.Params.name}}`. A missing key is an error,
never an empty string.
